correctness.rationale: Translation gives A^k=ka+kB with 0 in B; the chain of kB is strictly increasing until it fills H=<B>. Its least full index is exactly the monogenic index, and the eventual quotient-coset order is exactly the period. For index mu>=2, |H| >= |B|+mu-1 >= mu+1 and lambda divides |G/H|. Equalities force B={0,b}, cyclic H of order mu+1 and cyclic quotient generated by a+H. The direct cyclic construction attains the bound. For mu=1 the singleton generator yields minimum lambda. Exhaustive finite checks of 13,309 subsets across 17 group profiles and 130 constructions supplement the proof; all boundary cases were addressed.

originality.rationale: The full texts inspected for the recent embeddability problem, the 1979 finite-commutative representation reduction, and a contemporary survey do not give the exact least finite abelian host for every monogenic index and period, nor the complete equality normal form. Searches using index-period, cyclic semigroup, subset powers, and sumset stabilization terminology found no exact or dominating claim. This is a positive, bounded literature comparison rather than proof of global novelty; two plausible papers were not fully accessible.
residual_risks: The full text of Bershadsky–Kublanovsky (2025) was not accessible; a hidden equivalent result remains possible.
The full text of Pedersen–Sizer (1980) was not accessible; a historical result on cyclic subsemigroups may overlap.

Classical growth lemmas make parts of the proof elementary; the assessment of mathematical value rests on the sharp all-parameter host-order invariant and complete extremal normal form, not on sophistication of individual steps.

value.rationale: Least finite abelian host order is a natural exact resource invariant for the monogenic case of the power-semigroup embeddability programme. An all-index-period sharp formula, a universal cyclic attaining host, and a necessary-and-sufficient classification of all optimal generating subsets together constitute a natural complete extremal classification rather than an isolated construction or finite census.
